TRANSCRIPT OF PROCEEDINGS
THE HON CATHERINE HOLMES AC SC, Commissioner
THE ROYAL COMMISSION INTO THE ROBODEBT SCHEME
TUESDAY, 13 DECEMBER 2022 AT 10.01 AM (AEST)
DAY 19
MR JUSTIN GREGGERY KC, Senior Counsel Assisting
MR D. FREEBURN, Counsel Assisting
MS DOMINIQUE HOGAN-DORAN SC, for the Commonwealth
MR TRENT GLOVER, for the Commonwealth
MR JAMES ARNOTT SC, for Senator the Hon. Marise Payne

COMMISSIONER: Yes, Mr Greggery.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. Thank you, Commissioner. Today I appear with Mr Freeburn. There will
be three witnesses who give evidence: The Honourable Senator Marise Payne, who will
commence; then Ms Colleen Taylor, then employee of the Department of Human Services, at
least at January 2017, who gives information about process within the Department and her
correspondence with the Secretary; and, thirdly, Mr Anthony Barford, an employee of the
Department of Social Services during the relevant period as a member of the Debt Policy
team. Do you have a copy of the exhibit list before we move to the additional appearances?
COMMISSIONER: I do.
MR GREGGERY: It's convenient at this stage to tender the list of exhibits commencing 2491
through to 2555, which are all the exhibits for the day.
COMMISSIONER: Thank you. Those documents will be admitted as exhibits with the numbers
they bear in the schedule.
<EXHIBITS 2491 TO 2555 TENDERED
COMMISSIONER: Ms Hogan-Doran - I'm sorry, I'm just used to Ms Hogan-Doran next. You're
back with us?
MS HOGAN-DORAN: I am back. Thank you, Commissioner. I appear this morning with Mr
Glover of counsel.
COMMISSIONER: Yes. And -
MR ARNOTT: (Indistinct)
COMMISSIONER: And you need your microphone on. Thank you. Yes. Senator Payne, will you
take - you're calling Senator Payne, Mr Greggery?
MR GREGGERY: I am, yes.
COMMISSIONER: Will you take an oath or an affirmation?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: An affirmation, Commissioner.
COMMISSIONER: Thank you. Would you mind standing and that will just be administered.
<MARISE ANN PAYNE, AFFIRMED
<EXAMINATION BY MR GREGGERY:

COMMISSIONER: Thank you. Yes, Mr Greggery.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. Thank you. Senator Payne, you were issued with a Notice to Give a
Statement and Produce Documents, identified as NTG-0032, dated 18 October 2022?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes, Mr Greggery.
MR GREGGERY: And you produced two Statements in response, one dated 18 November
2022 and the second after you were provided additional documents by the Australian
Government Solicitor dated 9 December 2022?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: That's correct.
MR GREGGERY: And in those Statements, you refer to various documents and there are
others which have come to your attention in the recent days?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes, that's correct.
MR GREGGERY: Thank you. If I go back to the start, you were elected to the Senate in 1997?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: And you have remained continuously elected to the Senate since that time?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes, I have.
MR GREGGERY: In 2013, you took on the role of the Minister for Human Services?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Specifically, 18 September 2013?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: That's correct.
MR GREGGERY: And you held that position through until 21 September 2015?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: And you were then appointed as the Minister for the Defence and to other
Ministries subsequently?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: In your capacity as Minister for Human Services, you had regular interaction
with the Secretary and Senior Executive Service within that Department?

MR GREGGERY: And during this period of time, the Secretary was Ms Kathryn Campbell?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: That's right.
MR GREGGERY: In December 2014, that is, after you had been in the position for a little over
12 months, Minister Morrison was appointed to the position of the Minister for the Social
Services portfolio?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: And as between you and him, he being the portfolio Minister, was the senior
Minister?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: That's correct.
MR GREGGERY: As it's designated?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: And in fact.
MR GREGGERY: And that meant that you were not automatically a member of Cabinet in the
position that you held?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: I was not a member of Cabinet at all.
MR GREGGERY: And Mr Morrison was?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: That's correct.
MR GREGGERY: Irrespective of whether you were - that is, despite the fact you were not a
member of Cabinet, there were occasions when you attended Cabinet meetings, specifically
Expenditure Review Committee meetings from time to time as required?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: I think I would recall perhaps the instance that is the
subject of this discussion and few others. For junior Ministers in portfolios to attend Cabinet
or ERC, the opportunity doesn't arise that often.
MR GREGGERY: And in what circumstances does it arise?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: If you have specific portfolio responsibility for a
measure which may be coming before the Cabinet or the Cabinet Subcommittee, it relies on
you being called into the room in a timely manner. I have been outside the Cabinet room,
been called and entered the room and had the matter already dealt with before I entered
the room. So it depends on each circumstance.
MR GREGGERY: When there was an aspect of portfolio responsibility, would that concept

SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: You outline in your Statement, Ms Payne, that you went on leave 24
December - that's Christmas Eve 2014 - through to 9 January 2015 inclusive?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: That is, Friday, 9 January 2015. And when you returned the following week,
there was the first of a series of meetings which related to what was ultimately a New Policy
Proposal introduced in the 2014/2015 Budget, which was a portfolio responsibility of yours?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: That is, Mr Greggery, to the best of my recollection,
aided by access to my calendar and some notes, a number of meetings at the
commencement of the new year, which included consideration of this issue, but also many
other matters.
MR GREGGERY: And to get to the point, your recollection of your involvement in this
particular proposal is limited largely to the content of the documents that you've been able
to review at the time?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Given the effluxion of time, which is almost eight years,
that is correct, yes.
MR GREGGERY: Before you went on leave, you signed a letter to Mr Morrison which really
introduced him to the portfolio and offered that your Secretary, that is, Ms Campbell, would
meet him during the break or at a time convenient to him?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: That's correct, yes.
MR GREGGERY: If you could have Exhibit 2497 produced, CTH.3732.0001.008. This is the
letter. Ms Payne, this is one of the documents that you've had the opportunity to view in
your preparation?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes, that's correct.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. The overview of the Department is set out over the various pages, and
in the fourth substantive paragraph on that page you identify the arrangement that was
proposed between Ms Campbell and Mr Morrison to brief him on key priorities and
challenges for the Department?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: That was.
MR GREGGERY: And if we could go to the second page, please, ending 0009. And the
priorities for 2015, including the first substantive paragraph after subparagraph (a), could be
called out.

SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes, I can see the paragraph.
MR GREGGERY: You can see the paragraph.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. What is identified there is that:
The Department had a number of measures which it was due to implement to commence on
1 January 2015.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: On the previous Budget, that's right.
MR GREGGERY: On the previous Budget. That's right. But there remains a number of other
measures that await passage. Are you referring there to measures that await passage
through the Senate?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Through the Parliament, broadly speaking. I can't
specify which measures they were now. But, yes, that would be the normal language that
would be used.
MR GREGGERY: The composition of the Senate at that time - this may be something you can
recall independently, but try and be specific about it. Of the 76 Senate seats, the Coalition
had 33 and the Labor Party had 25. The Greens had 10. The Palmer United Party had 1. There
were four independents: one representative of the Liberal Democratic Party; one Family First
representative; and one Senator from the Australian Motoring Enthusiast Party?
COMMISSIONER: Are you sure about Palmer United, Mr Greggery? I thought there were
three. Perhaps it doesn't matter very much, but -
MR GREGGERY: My total comes to 76.
COMMISSIONER: Alright. Well, it must be right, then.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: I think, Commissioner, they may have left the Palmer
United Party at different times.
COMMISSIONER: That's true. They came and went.
MR GREGGERY: They may form - of the four independents, they may have originally been
some additional members of the Palmer United Party.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: I don't recall the exact timing, but it is possible.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. Alright.

SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: And I had forgotten about the Australian Motoring
Enthusiasts.
MR GREGGERY: And in terms of the numbers on the crossbench, that was a record number
of 18 at that time, at least in your experience in the Senate?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: I will agree with you, Mr Greggery. I don't have a precise
recall of every formation of every Senate of which I've been a part -
MR GREGGERY: No.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: - right now here.
MR GREGGERY: Of course. And I don't expect you to. But the short point is that measures
awaiting passage through the Parliament generally reflected in part the difficulty faced by
the Coalition -
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Indeed.
MR GREGGERY: - passing legislation through the Senate.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Indeed.
MR GREGGERY: If we can go down to the bottom paragraph and ask that it be pulled out,
please. There was a broad statement in this paragraph, Ms Payne, that the Department was
working with DSS to develop New Policy Proposals and cost estimates for the '15/16 Budget.
And if I pause there, there was nothing unusual about that concept. There were reviews
regularly undertaken in anticipation of annual Budgets and Mid-Year Economic and Fiscal
Outlooks -
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: That's correct. Yes.
MR GREGGERY: - that would fall within that category or within that description?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: In terms of the Coalition position in respect of the Budget, there was a
general approach that sought to deliver a balanced Budget over a number of years at about
this time. You would agree with that?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: And one aspect of that was obviously identifying areas of savings or potential
savings?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: That's right.

MR GREGGERY: The other, of course, is reducing expenditure in broad terms?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: When you then returned from leave - perhaps Monday, 12 January - you
soon thereafter, that is, the following day, Tuesday, 13 January 2015, met with the Secretary,
Ms Campbell, and your Chief of Staff. You have been able to identify an entry in your diary
which suggests that? Sorry, in your calendar?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes, we have exacted as many of those as we could for
the Commission.
MR GREGGERY: Thank you. And if I could go then to Exhibit 2499. This is your diary note of
that meeting, Ms Payne. Thank you. And just to confirm with you, a number of matters were
discussed between yourself and the Secretary that day. But if we go to the second page, the
relevant passage for the purpose of this inquiry commences with the phrase "Minister
Morrison" about five lines down.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes, I can see that.
MR GREGGERY: And what you've written there - thank you:
Minister Morrison - compliance; focus on integrity of system and integrity of outlays; NPP,
compliance now/options for...
"Future" is it?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: "Further".
MR GREGGERY: "Further". And NPP in that context refers to New Policy Proposal?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Again -
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: I presume so, yes.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. Alright.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: And it's in the margin. Whether it's a follow-up note to
myself or whether it was part of the discussion, I can't now recall specifically.
MR GREGGERY: In a general sense, do you recall from this meeting that Ms Campbell
informed you she had met with Minister Morrison over the Christmas break, and he had
asked her to prepare some proposals about the current integrity of the welfare system and
what might be done in terms of the future?

SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: I can't specifically say that I recall the meeting itself.
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: What I can say from its timing in my calendar and my
own notes is that that would seem to be the case and that the Secretary would have
explained to me - or detailed to me, I should say, her meeting with Minister Morrison in that
discussion on 13 January.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. What flows from this meeting is a number of Briefings or draft Briefings
to you, which were consistent with - from your review of the documents - and I appreciate
your limited recollection. But from your limited recollection and the review of the
documents, a series of Briefings provided to you by the Department of Human Services is
consistent with your recollection that Minister Morrison had - Minister Morrison asked DHS,
that is, through Ms Campbell, to outline the approach of DHS to protecting the integrity of
the welfare system outlays and options for strengthening it?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: I think that's an accurate assessment, yes.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. And that appeared to be the crux of what you noted in this meeting?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: In - specifically in relation to the Secretary's meeting
with Minister Morrison, yes.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. That's right. If I could have Exhibit 2500, CTH.3784.0001.0002. Ms
Payne, this was a - the first of a series of briefings prepared by the Department of Human
Services. It is signed by Ms Golightly, the Deputy Secretary, 15 January, and identified at the
top is the critical date of 20 January '15. And the reason is identified as a discussion at a
meeting with the Secretary and the General Manager of Business Integrity and, it seems,
Ms Golightly, which was anticipated for the 20th.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: I believe so, yes.
MR GREGGERY: Now, again, being briefed in this form was a very regular process within the
Department, perhaps the primary record of communication between the Department and
the Minister's Office?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: And in my experience, across all Departments, yes.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. The introduction on the covering letter identifies the recent meeting
between Ms Campbell and Minister Morrison and the request to prepare a Brief on current
compliance processes and options for improvement. And that was, again, the continuation of
the context which you gleaned from the meeting a few days earlier?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.

MR GREGGERY: The attachment was a draft Brief and proposals, which appears as Exhibit
2501, and we might turn to that, CTH.3784.0001.0004. Thank you. And can I confirm what
appeared from the previous document, that it was not signed by you or marked by you, and
that was because it was discussed in the meeting on 20 February and returned to the
Department unsigned and then further Briefings were developed?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: It's certainly, to the extent of the material that's been
made available to me, not signed by me and not marked by me.
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: I can't say that that is because it was discussed at the
meeting because I don't recall whether or not this was put in front of me or whether the
issues were discussed. And, Mr Greggery, that is, again, an effort to recollect over seven
years a past meeting. So I can't - I can't agree that it was because of that fact. But I do know
that I have clearly, on the material available to me, not signed it or annotated it in any way.
And I don't specifically recall it.
MR GREGGERY: I appreciate that. The only document which might shed some light on this is
Exhibit 2517. It's not your document. CTH.3043.0069.2611. It was produced by the
Department, I think, and I understand that it was included in your bundle. The -
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: I saw that this morning.
MR GREGGERY: This morning.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: This piece this morning.
MR GREGGERY: This piece this morning. Yes. It's the first entry here, B-15/39, Current
Compliance Processes and Options. The record in the right column - and, again, I understand
it's not your document - simply says that:
Parliamentary Services advised Ministers Office...
That's MO?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: That's not a direct reference to you; it's to the office?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: No.
MR GREGGERY:
...requested unsigned Brief be returned as Minister Payne provided her feedback directly to
the Secretary, Deputy Secretary and GM at their meeting.

SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: I see the note, but I can't add anything further. I'm
sorry.
MR GREGGERY: Thank you.
MR ARNOTT: Commissioner, could I just note in relation to this document, which we were
provided this morning, that the metadata that we have been given suggests it was produced
on - created in September 2020, just after Senator Payne had left the portfolio.
COMMISSIONER: Sure. I don't think it's suggested that it was contentious.
MR ARNOTT: No, I didn't understand that to be the tenor of the question, but I just wanted
to make that point.
COMMISSIONER: Thank you.
MR GREGGERY: Senator Payne, you were able to identify from your electronic diary an entry
relating to a meeting with Ms Campbell, Ms Golightly and Mr Withnell on 20 January 2015?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: That's correct.
MR GREGGERY: And you were able to locate notes from your diary about that meeting?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. Taking those in sequence, the first is 2502, MPA.0001.0001.0086.
That's the calendar entry that you were able to locate or was located for you?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes, that's correct.
MR GREGGERY: Thank you. And the next is Exhibit 2503, MPA.0001.0002.0085. Sorry. It
might form part of the same exhibit, then. There's a subsequent page. No, 0002.0085.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes, I have that.
MR GREGGERY: You have that. I will just wait for it, I think. Yes. For the document manager,
there is a different number to the exhibit on the screen, and the centre four digits end in
0002. I have been given the indication it's not far away. Yes. This is the diary entry in respect
of that meeting, Senator Payne?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Notebook entry, yes.
MR GREGGERY: Notebook entry. Secretary, that's a reference to Ms Campbell?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: That's correct.

SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: And MW, Mark Withnell?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: That's right.
MR GREGGERY: The entry says:
This Data-matching Act - FR '93.
And then:
Broad - not a strict liability offence: Q of intent? 12 times AFP. List of 1 January changes.
This is the extent, I take it, of any records you made of the meeting and what was discussed?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: That is correct. We've provided all of that to the
Commission.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. The minute which we referred to previously, B-15/39, is a document you
have reviewed in preparation for your Statement?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Perhaps -
MR GREGGERY: I will take you back to it.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: - since my Statement.
MR GREGGERY: Since your Statement.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: It may have been reviewed since my Statement. It might
not have been available at the time of my Statement.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. I understand the documents, I think, came through the Australian
Government Solicitor to your solicitor relatively recently.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: In tranches, I would describe it as. But I have seen the
document, yes. It's the one we were just talking about just earlier.
MR GREGGERY: It is, yes.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: If we could return to - sorry, before we do that, "Data-matching Act - FR
'93", is that from 1993?

SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes, Mr Greggery. In my shorthand, that is "from". And I
think that is a reference to the date of Act, but actually the Act is, as I now understand, a
1990 Act. So I'm not sure. Perhaps it was amended in 1993. I don't know.
MR GREGGERY: It reflects at least the topic of the Data-matching Act -
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Correct.
MR GREGGERY: - was discussed in the meeting?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: I - I can't say with absolute confidence because I don't
recall the details of the discussion, but obviously I've made a notation, yes.
MR GREGGERY: If we return then to Exhibit 2501, CTH.3784.0001.0004. This is the
attachment to B-15/39.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Thank you. I think that screen indicates that the previous document hadn't
been uploaded yet and so they're moving in and out of the system. The attachment to
B-15/39 is addressed to the Minister for Social Services for action, that is, Mr Morrison?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes. That's correct.
MR GREGGERY: And it refers in paragraph 1 to the recent meeting between Ms Campbell and
Mr Morrison where the Department was asked to prepare a Brief which contained the points
in subparagraphs (a) and (b). Now, in terms of your review of this document in the last few
days, and your review of other versions or subsequent Briefings, were you able to identify
that the document in some respects was rewritten from - following the meeting of 20
January 2015 but in other respects some of the core features remained the same?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: If I was to - if I was to consider how it progressed from
this document to its next version -
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: - I would say that this is a lengthy document.
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: That when Briefing to the Cabinet Minister, it is
desirable to be concise, tight, clear. Whether it's coming from the Department or from, in my
case, via a junior Minister. And that that may reflect the change - at least part of the changes
in terms of length of the document.
MR GREGGERY: Yes.

SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: But, again, I say that for context and what my
experience has been in such matters. I don't have a specific recollection in relation to the
changes from this particular document to its next one. But that is context in terms of how
the approach might be made.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. If we could go to the page ending 0014, and I will just take you
through some of the content of this draft. I accept what you say earlier - or acknowledge
what you say earlier about not having any independent recollection of reading this or what
was communicated to you orally in the meeting, but I will come to some of the specific
content shortly.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: So I have a different number - I see. Sorry.
MR GREGGERY: That's fine. It is Attachment B to the -
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: That's 0011 on the top and 0014 below it. I'm sorry.
MR GREGGERY: Your document has two numbers. Yes, that occurs sometimes. You just
described the process of a proposal or a Briefing coming through the junior Minister, and
we're about to go through a number of the versions of the draft. What role did you have to
play as the junior Minister in response to Mr Morrison's request of Ms Campbell?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: A junior Minister in a portfolio would be working with
and encourage their Department - and this is a slightly unique situation to the extent that the
portfolio contains two separate Departments - standalone Departments - would, as I said,
encourage and work with the Department to produce the material that had been requested
in response to the Cabinet Minister's meeting - the meeting with the Cabinet Minister, with
my Secretary. And I would expect that to include engagement with my staff, with me from
time to time. But overwhelmingly, the work is done within the Department and led by the
appropriate member of the SES.
MR GREGGERY: That is, to whomever the Secretary delegated the primary task, if not
performed by the Secretary?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes. Except that the delegation becomes, to a degree,
obvious because of the various policy area responsibilities of the members of the SES.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. The question of policy in terms of Ministerial responsibility, that is, your
Ministerial responsibility, was conferred by Administrative Arrangement Orders -
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: - at successive periods?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.

MR GREGGERY: And you refer in your Statement to policy responsibility for implementation.
That's something that you understood from the responsibilities conferred by the relevant
Administrative Arrangement Order at the time?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Broadly speaking. So the delivery of the payment
system.
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Those sorts of delivery aspects, yes.
MR GREGGERY: And did you understand that responsibility to extend to this particular
measure in the sense that it created - not only ultimately was it a Budget Measure, but
because it emanated from the Department and related to the calculation of overpayments
for recipients of social security benefits?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes, because compliance and integrity were core
business for the Department of Human Services in the making of payments to ensure that
the right people were being paid the right amount; people were not able to defraud the
Commonwealth if they set out to do so; and that where incorrect payments were made, no
matter where the error lay, that they could be corrected.
MR GREGGERY: And the use of the word "integrity" relates to either overpayments or
deliberate fraud in that sense?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Yes.
COMMISSIONER: It seems to be used generally by the Department as if it were
interchangeable with "accuracy", Ms Payne. Is that right?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Commissioner, I've not seen it used in that way in the
context of my preparation with these documents for this Royal Commission.
Accuracy - accuracy is on both sides of the coin, for both the recipient of the payment and
the Department as the issuing body.
COMMISSIONER: It's just that generally one wouldn't think of correctness of payments as
being a matter of integrity, which most people would see as something else altogether. But it
seems to be used quite freely in all this material.
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Commissioner, I think it may - may be when the
accuracy of payment relies on the - relies at least in part on the recipient providing their
details as to their circumstances to enable the payment to be accurate. And when there is
certainly a cohort that's referred to in these documents, a cohort of people who don't do
that, then accuracy and integrity can, in fact, be directly linked. But I have not seen all of this
evidence and so I don't want to speculate.

SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Thank you.
MR GREGGERY: In your experience as Minister for the Department, were you aware that
there were also administrative errors or administrative inaccuracy in the delivery of social
security payments?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: From time to time, yes, because the Department is
staffed by over 30,000 people and they are not free of human error.
MR GREGGERY: That's right. And at least -
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: All of us.
MR GREGGERY: At least accuracy was used in that sense -
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: Certainly.
MR GREGGERY: - to describe the delivery of payments on the part of the Department?
SENATOR THE HON. MARISE PAYNE: I would believe so, yes.
MR GREGGERY: The - Senator Payne, this is the first iteration of the potential New Policy
